extracted.intended_audience: applicants, licensees, carriers, and counsel involved in FCC Wireless Radio Services filings and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for preparing, filing, and maintaining applications, reports, records, and related notifications for stations and carriers in the FCC Wireless Radio Services under 47 CFR Part 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extension of filing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of time within which to file contracts, reports, and requests referred to in §§ 1.783 through 1.814 shall be made in writing and may be granted for good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to extensions for filing contracts, reports, and requests listed in §§ 1.783–1.814; burden is on requester to show good cause; requests must be written.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of carrier contracts (§ 1.783)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of carrier contracts, agreements, concessions, licenses, authorizations or other arrangements, shall be filed as required by part 43 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carrier contractual documents must be submitted per the filing rules of part 43; check part 43 for format/timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual financial reports (Form M) (§ 1.785)
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual financial report shall be filed by telephone carriers and affiliates as required by part 43 of this chapter on form M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires verified copies of SEC Form 10‑K (or equivalent) to be filed annually; separate supplemental annual reports required where carrier and non-carrier operations are separate departments or divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports of proposed changes in depreciation rates (§ 1.787)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers shall file reports regarding proposed changes in depreciation rates as required by part 43 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing follows part 43 procedures and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports relating to international traffic (§ 1.790)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers shall file periodic reports regarding international point-to-point traffic as required by part 43 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow part 43 for periodicity and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports and requests under part 32 (§ 1.791)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and requests shall be filed either periodically, upon the happening of specified events, or for specific approval by telephone companies in accordance with and subject to the provisions of part 32 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe part 32 triggers and filing mechanisms for required submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports regarding interstate rates of return (§ 1.795)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers shall file reports regarding interstate rates of return on FCC Form 492 as required by part 65 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FCC Form 492 and follow part 65 instructions and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports for continuing authority / temporary or emergency service (§ 1.802)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers receiving authority under part 63 of this chapter shall file quarterly or semiannual reports as required therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow reporting frequency and content specified in part 63 for authorities granted thereunder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports on reduction in temporary experimental service (§ 1.803)
rubrics_metrics.description: As required in part 63 of this chapter, carriers shall report reductions in service which had previously been expanded on an experimental basis for a temporary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit required reports consistent with part 63 provisions governing experimental/temporary expansions and reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports regarding free service rendered the Government (§ 1.814)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers rendering free service in connection with the national defense to any agency of the United States Government shall file reports in accordance with part 2 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow part 2 reporting procedures for free services rendered to government agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual employment reports (FCC Form 395) (§ 1.815)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each common carrier licensee or permittee with 16 or more full time employees shall file with the Commission, on or before May 31 of each year, on FCC Form 395, an annual employment report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of reports, exhibits, letters and related correspondence filed are open for public inspection at Commission offices; see cross-references for EEO applicability to certain facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence of Part 1 rules (§ 1.902)
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of any conflict between the rules set forth in this subpart and the rules set forth in [listed parts], the rules in this part shall govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple parts conflict, Part 1's rules take precedence for matters covered by this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization required for operation (§ 1.903)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stations in the Wireless Radio Services must be used and operated only in accordance with the rules applicable to their particular service and with a valid authorization granted by the Commission under the provisions of this part, except as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizations granted only if applicant is qualified (citizenship, character, financial, technical and other criteria) and public interest, convenience and necessity will be served; holding an authorization does not create rights beyond terms, conditions, and period specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber authorization rules (§ 1.903(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority for subscribers to operate mobile or fixed stations in the Wireless Radio Services is included in the authorization held by the licensee providing service; the Commission does not accept applications from subscribers for individual mobile or fixed station authorizations in the Wireless Radio Services, with specific exceptions noted in service rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See service-specific sections for exceptions (e.g., rural subscriber stations, certain SMR systems, ships/aircraft under parts 80 and 87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Antenna structure (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term antenna structure includes the radiating and receiving elements, its supporting structures, towers, and all appurtenances mounted thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when determining obligations such as registration, environmental review, and antenna-specific application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Application (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request on a standard form for a station license ... signed in accordance with § 1.917, or a similar request to amend a pending application or to modify or renew an authorization; includes requests to assign rights or transfer control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers initial, amendment, modification, renewal, assignment, transfer, and related requests—applies to signature and filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Auctionable license / application (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auctionable license: a Wireless Radio Service license identified in § 1.2102 for which competitive bidding is used. Auctionable license application: an application for such a license where competitive bidding is used if subject to mutual exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for auctionable licenses must comply with subpart Q and auction-specific orders/public notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Authorization (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written instrument or oral statement issued by the FCC conveying authority to operate, for a specified term, to a station in the Wireless Telecommunications Services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizations set authorized bandwidth, power, and terms under which stations must operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Authorized bandwidth / power (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized bandwidth: the maximum bandwidth permitted to be used by a station as specified in the station license. Authorized power: the maximum power a station is permitted to use as specified by the Commission in the authorization or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must observe and request appropriate bandwidth and power as authorized; used in coordination and interference determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — ERP and EIRP (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective radiated power (ERP): the product of the power supplied to the antenna multiplied by the gain of the antenna referenced to a half-wave dipole. Equivalent Isotropically Radiated Power (EIRP): the product of the power supplied to the antenna multiplied by the antenna gain referenced to an isotropic antenna.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct metric (ERP vs EIRP) as specified by service rules and application forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Control station, fixed station, mobile station (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control station: a fixed station whose transmissions are used to control other stations; Fixed station: a station operating at a fixed location; Mobile station: a radio communication station capable of being moved and which ordinarily does move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate station type on forms and in showings; different rules and authorizations may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — Covered geographic and covered site-based licenses (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of services that constitute 'covered geographic licenses' and 'covered site-based licenses' used for particular Part 1 subparts (enumerates many services and parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether a license is covered geographic or site-based to identify applicable auction and processing rules in subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — Non-auctionable license / application (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-auctionable license: a service license for which competitive bidding is not used. Non-auctionable license application: an application precluded from competitive bidding under § 1.2102 if subject to mutual exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow non-auction processing rules when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — Spectrum leasing arrangement / lessee (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectrum leasing arrangement: an arrangement where a licensee leases certain spectrum usage rights to a spectrum lessee as set in subpart X. Spectrum lessee: any third-party entity that leases such rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectrum leasing is regulated by subpart X (47 CFR 1.9001 et seq.); certain filings/notifications (e.g., FCC Form 608) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Universal Licensing System (ULS) (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: ULS is the consolidated database, application filing system, and processing system for all Wireless Radio Services; supports electronic filing and public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ULS is the official filing channel for covered services; check ULS instructions for electronic filing and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — Wireless Radio Services and Wireless Telecommunications Services (§ 1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wireless Radio Services: all radio services authorized in listed parts. Wireless Telecommunications Services: Wireless Radio Services that meet the definition of 'telecommunications service' under 47 U.S.C. 153 and are regulated as common carrier services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines regulatory classification and applicability of common carrier requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station files maintained in ULS (§ 1.911)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, notifications, correspondence, electronic filings and other material ... comprising technical, legal, and administrative data relating to each station are maintained by the Commission in ULS. These files constitute the official records and supersede any other records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ULS records are the authoritative source—ensure accurate filings and attachments in ULS because they form the official station file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application and notification forms (§ 1.913(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, licensees, and spectrum lessees shall use specified forms and associated schedules (FCC Forms 601, 602, 603, 605, 608, 609) for all applications and notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form has specific uses (e.g., Form 601 for authorizations, Form 602 for ownership, Form 603 for assignment/transfer, Form 605 for certain quick-form authorizations, Form 608 for spectrum leasing, Form 609 for eligibility events). Use the correct form/schedule for each filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement (§ 1.913(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified elsewhere, all applications and other filings using the application and notification forms must be filed electronically in accordance with ULS electronic filing instructions. For mandatory services, effective July 1, 1999 or six months after ULS deployment for the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload attachments with the application when possible; files other than ASCII TOC should be PDF whenever possible; the Commission will announce deployment dates for each service in ULS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments and associated documents (§ 1.913(b)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments to applications and notifications should be uploaded along with electronically filed applications and notifications whenever possible. Files (other than ASCII table of contents) and associated documents should be in PDF whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure attachments are uploaded via ULS as PDF to be accepted and associated with the relevant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auctioned license applications compliance (§ 1.913(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Auctioned license applications shall also comply with the requirements of subpart Q of this part and applicable Commission orders and public notices issued with respect to each auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult auction-specific public notices and subpart Q for bidding, eligibility, and filing requirements in addition to Part 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications requiring prior frequency coordination (§ 1.913(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties filing applications that require frequency coordination shall, prior to filing, complete all applicable frequency coordination requirements in service-specific rules. After appropriate coordination, such applications must be filed electronically via ULS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed by frequency coordinator on applicant's behalf, must be filed electronically; complete coordination steps before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications for amateur licenses and VE procedures (§ 1.913(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for amateur radio operator licenses that require passing exam elements must present Volunteer Examiners (VEs) with all information required; VEs may collect information in any manner; upon completion, VEs issue CSCE and send info to Volunteer-Examiner Coordinator (VEC); applications filed with Commission by VECs and other amateur applications must be filed electronically via ULS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feeable vanity call sign requests follow § 0.401 or electronic filing via ULS; VEs/VECs handle pre-filing examination steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 337 public safety request filing (§ 1.913(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to provide public safety services submitted pursuant to 47 U.S.C. 337 must be filed on the same form and in the same manner as other applications for the requested frequencies, except applicants must select the service code reflective of the type of service intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow normal application form/process but use appropriate service code for public safety designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General application requirement (§ 1.915(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (b), for all Wireless Radio Services, station licenses, operator licenses, modifications or renewals, assignments or transfers of control, and waiver requests associated with any of the foregoing shall be granted only upon an application filed pursuant to §§ 1.913 through 1.917.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed forms and follow §§ 1.913–1.917 unless an exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency filing exceptions (§ 1.915(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may grant station licenses or modifications/renewals without formal application in emergencies (danger to life/property, national emergency, or where not feasible to secure renewal applications). No such authorization continues beyond the period of the emergency or war; procedures for emergency requests are same as for special temporary authority under § 1.931; after emergency, party must submit appropriate FCC form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency authorizations are temporary and must be followed by formal application once feasible; do not rely on emergency grants beyond the emergency period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign applications (§ 1.917(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, amendments, and related statements of fact must be signed by: the applicant (individual); one partner (partnership); an officer, director, or duly authorized employee (corporation); a member officer (unincorporated association); trustee (amateur radio club). Applications by government entities must be signed by an authorized elected/appointed official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the signer has proper authority under entity type; signatures can be manual or electronic as defined in paragraph (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney or vessel master signature exceptions (§ 1.917(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be signed by the applicant's attorney in case of the applicant's physical disability or absence from the United States, or by the designated vessel master when a temporary permit is requested for a vessel. The attorney must set forth the reason why not signed by applicant and state reasons for beliefs where matters are stated on belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the original need be signed; attorney/master must provide explanatory statements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: False statements and oath (§ 1.917(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, amendments, and related statements of fact need not be signed under oath; willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and can result in administrative sanctions including revocation under Communications Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy is mandatory; even without oath, false statements have criminal and administrative consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature definition (§ 1.917(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Signed' for manual filings means original hand-written signature; for electronic filings, an electronic signature consists of the name of the applicant transmitted electronically via ULS or any other electronic filing interface the Commission may designate and entered on the application as a signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing electronically, include the applicant name in the signature field as the legal electronic signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership information and use of FCC Form 602 (§ 1.919)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants or licensees in Wireless Radio Services subject to ownership reporting requirements of § 1.2112 shall use FCC Form 602 to provide all ownership information required by the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 602 must be filed/updated at times specified (initial application, renewal, assignment/transfer, notification of consummation, reportable eligibility events); one Form 602 can be associated with multiple applications; no filing fee required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and circumstances to file/update Form 602 (§ 1.919(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: File FCC Form 602 or update it at time of: (1) initial application (Form 601); (2) license renewal (Form 601); (3) assignment/transfer application (Form 603); (4) notification of consummation of pro forma assignment/transfer (Form 603); (5) application reporting any reportable eligibility event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a current Form 602 is already on file, applicant may certify that it's current instead of filing a new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure obligations for applicants not subject to § 1.2112 (§ 1.919(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants or licensees not subject to ownership reporting requirements of § 1.2112 are not required to file FCC Form 602; however, they may be required by rules applicable to such services to disclose the real party (or parties) in interest, including complete disclosure of identity and relationships of persons/entities owning or controlling the applicant or licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not subject to § 1.2112, check service rules for disclosure obligations of real parties in interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications must contain all requested information (§ 1.923(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must contain all information requested on the applicable form and any additional information required by the rules in this chapter and any rules pertaining to the specific service for which the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete forms or omitted required information can be cause for rejection or requests for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference conditions (§ 1.923(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may incorporate information already on file by reference provided: (1) referenced information has been filed in ULS or, if manually filed outside ULS, comprises more than one 8½×11 page; (2) referenced information is current and accurate in all material respects; and (3) the application states specifically where the referenced information can actually be found (station call sign or file number and location, or title/docket number/legal citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on incorporation by reference, give precise pointers and ensure referenced material is accessible and current; do not use reference as substitute for required application answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antenna location description requirement (§ 1.923(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for stations at fixed locations must describe each transmitting antenna site by its geographical coordinates and also by its street address, or by reference to a nearby landmark. Geographical coordinates, referenced to NAD83, must be specified in degrees, minutes, and seconds to the nearest second of latitude and longitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide NAD83 coordinates to the nearest second and give street address or landmark; essential for licensing, coordination, and environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antenna structure registration and temporary acceptance (§ 1.923(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications proposing use of antenna structures must contain the FCC Antenna Structure Registration Number(s) for each structure for which registration is required. The Bureau will accept an application that does not contain the Antenna Structure Registration Number so long as: (1) the owner has filed an FCC Form 854; (2) owner has provided local notice and Commission posted notification pursuant to § 17.4(c)(3) and (4); and (3) owner has obtained a Determination of No Hazard from FAA. Applicant shall provide the FCC Form 854 File Number and later amend the application to provide the Antenna Structure Registration Number; Commission will not grant application before AST Registration Number provided. If registration not required, applicant must provide information sufficient for Commission to verify this fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume an application will be granted without eventual antenna registration; follow Form 854 process and provide necessary notifications and FAA determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental processing and Environmental Assessments (§ 1.923(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental processing shall be completed pursuant to § 17.4(c) for any facilities that use antenna structures for which registration is required. For applications proposing facilities not subject to § 17.4(c), the applicant must indicate whether a grant may have a significant environmental effect per § 1.1307; if affirmative, an Environmental Assessment as required by § 1.1311 must be filed with the application and environmental review must be completed prior to construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trigger environmental review obligations early; file required EA with the application when potential significant effects exist and do not commence construction until review complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: International coordination requirement (§ 1.923(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel assignments and/or usage under this part are subject to provisions and requirements of treaties and other international agreements between the U.S. and the governments of Canada and Mexico.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure applications and assignments respect treaty obligations and coordination procedures with Canada/Mexico where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet Zone compliance (§ 1.923(g) and § 1.924)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant is required to comply with the 'Quiet Zone' rule. For specified quiet zones (NRAO/NRRO and Table Mountain), applicants planning to construct/operate new or modified stations within defined geographic areas must notify the relevant observatory/research entity in writing of technical details (coordinates, antenna height, directivity, channel, emission type and power). When an application is filed with the FCC, a 20‑day period for comments/objections follows notification; written consent from the quiet zone entity allows processing without awaiting the 20‑day period. If notification was made prior to filing, applicant must also provide notice upon actual filing. If objection is received, FCC will consider record and take appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely and complete technical notice to quiet zone entities, include notification dates in FCC application, and obtain written consent when possible to avoid delays. Specific procedures differ for services with different authorization schemes (see § 88.35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TINs) requirement (§ 1.923(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Wireless applicants and licensees, including all attributable owners of auctionable licenses as defined by § 1.2112, are required to provide their Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TINs) to the Commission pursuant to the Debt Collection Improvement Act of 1996. The Commission will not publicly disclose TINs unless authorized by law, but will assign a 'public identification number' for agency use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide TINs when required; the Commission may use TINs for debt collection; expect assignment of a public ID to protect TIN privacy in public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email address requirement for service (§ 1.923(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must specify an email address where the applicant can receive electronic correspondence. This email will be used to serve documents or direct correspondence; any correspondence sent to the email on file is deemed served. Applicants should also provide a USPS address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep email address current in ULS; electronic service to the address on file is effective service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Mountain quiet zone advisory (§ 1.924(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees and applicants planning to construct and operate a new or modified station at a permanent fixed location in the vicinity of Boulder County, Colorado are advised to give consideration, prior to filing applications, to the need to protect the Table Mountain Radio Receiving Zone from interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider interference mitigation and coordination for operations near Table Mountain; pre-filing coordination may avoid objections or processing delays.
